bio:
I am a research associate and software developer in the [Buckler Lab](https://www.maizegenetics.net/) at Cornell University, where I develop and maintain several widely used software libraries and web applications, including [TASSEL](https://www.maizegenetics.net/tassel), [ViDGER](https://github.com/btmonier/vidger), [IRIS-EDA](https://github.com/btmonier/iris), [rTASSEL](https://github.com/maize-genetics/rTASSEL), and [rPHG](https://github.com/maize-genetics/rPHG2).

My research interests span bioinformatics, scientific software development, and education. At the Buckler Lab, I have contributed to methods for efficiently assembling and annotating hundreds of wild grass relatives of maize and sorghum through the [PanAnd Project](https://www.panandropogoneae.org/). I have also collaborated with the ([now defunct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USAID_in_the_second_Trump_administration)) [Innovation Lab for Crop Improvement (ILCI)](https://cals.cornell.edu/global-development/feed-future-innovation-lab-for-crop-improvement), working with research institutions across Africa, the Caribbean, Latin America, and North America to design cloud computing infrastructure and scalable breeding pipelines. This work leveraged gene activity prediction models for sorghum, cowpea, cassava, rice, and maize, with an emphasis on delivering production-ready genomic analysis workflows.

My current research focuses on [pangenomics](https://github.com/maize-genetics/phg_v2) and [machine-learning imputation](https://github.com/maize-genetics/MLImpute) methods.

Prior to joining Cornell, my research centered on bioinformatics approaches to studying microbial interactions in next-generation lignocellulosic feedstocks and their impacts on biomass development.
